# Learnings and mistakes

No structural facts are generated for this page; the store has no concept of a mistake, only of records, decisions and handovers. Everything here is written by hand.

## Notes (human, preserved verbatim on regeneration)

<!-- bm-human:begin -->
## The measurement that changed the plan

Judged estimates were measured against actuals for the first time. At n=7 the
median is 3.75x fast, and the honest headline is the SPREAD, not the median:

    CALIBRATED clock=agent basis=judged n=7 median=3.75 min=0.66 max=5.33

Six tasks ran 3.0x to 5.3x faster than judged. ONE ran 0.66x, meaning slower.
That one was R1.1, forecast 45 minutes, actual 68, and it was the only task
that met a problem nobody had foreseen: the canonical Project shape refusing
the new fields. So the multiplier does not track task SIZE. It tracks how well
SPECIFIED the task is. An agent is roughly four times faster on work whose
files and done-check are already named, and at or below parity on work it has
to figure out first, because it pays full price for every wrong turn.

Applying one multiplier to everything would have been the old mistake with a
decimal point on it.

## Mistakes made, in the order they happened

1. **I ran the full gate against uncommitted work.** It refused to report
   green and listed my own files as suite pollution. Correct behaviour, wasted
   seventeen minutes. The gate runs against a COMMITTED tree, always.

2. **I registered the two new tools in four registries and missed the fifth.**
   SUITES, the CI workflow, the effect-class registry and the write-site
   inventory all got entries. pyproject.toml did not, so a `pip install` would
   have shipped neither tool. The gate caught it, I did not. My earlier check
   had grepped pyproject for TEST files and concluded it did not list them,
   which was true and irrelevant: it lists the TOOLS.

3. **I specified `datetime.utcnow()` in a builder brief.** It is deprecated
   from Python 3.12 and prints a warning to stderr on every call, beside a
   verdict line that gets read as a verdict. My error, not the builder's.

4. **I wrote a PASS line that said "all closed" while forecasts were open.**
   Also my specification. It is precisely the false reassurance the tool
   exists to remove.

5. **`pgrep -fl claude` dumped about forty thousand characters** of Electron
   argv into my context for an answer that needed one line. The existing memory
   note on this machine actually RECOMMENDED `pgrep -fl` as the safe listing
   step; it has been corrected. Agent argv carries the whole prompt, which
   makes broad pattern matching dangerous in both directions, killing and
   reading.

## Near misses

- **The first draft of my own R1.3 test failed, and was right to.** Run from a
  directory that is not a BrotherMode project, `detect` exits 0 and prints
  `NO-DATA: no BrotherMode project root found`. That is detect WORKING. My
  assertion list omitted it, so the test reported a wiring regression that had
  not happened. Had I trusted the test over the code I would have "fixed" a
  correct implementation.

- **A builder handed back a workaround honestly instead of hiding it.** R1.1
  carried the two new fields AROUND the canonical shape, popping them off the
  dict before `Project(**d)`. It said so plainly in its report. Had it not, that
  would have shipped as permanent debt in the one place this project cares most
  about.

- **The word "flake" nearly hid a real bug in the close ceremony itself.** A
  suite failed once in a gate run, would not reproduce in five isolated runs,
  and did not recur on the next. Everything pointed at noise. It was filed with
  its evidence rather than dismissed, and explicitly not called fixed, which is
  the only reason it got a second look when it recurred. It was a genuine
  defect in the tool that gates every session close: the zip freshness check
  compared the archive's BYTES, and a zip entry header carries each member's
  mtime, so a byte-identical re-save crossing an MS-DOS two second boundary
  read as a changed pack, about one run in forty. A previous finding, F9, had
  already tried to fix this exact path and had moved it from directory mtime to
  archive bytes, which is a real improvement that does not go far enough
  because zip bytes are not content. Fixed here by comparing a content
  fingerprint, with a deterministic test replacing the probabilistic one.

  The transferable lesson is not about zips. It is that "will not reproduce"
  is a description of the OBSERVATION, never a diagnosis, and the honest move
  is to write it down with its evidence and leave it open, which costs almost
  nothing and is what made the fix possible an hour later.
